metadata.note: The Detroit, Bay City and Alpena Railroad -- a name that, like the Frisco's promise of San Francisco, oversold its own reach: the DBC&A never owned track into either Detroit or Bay City. Its own rails ran only from a junction with the Michigan Central at Alger (in northwest Arenac County, ~40 miles from Bay City) north along the Lake Huron shore through the Tawas towns to Alpena, a lumber boomtown; travel to Detroit or Bay City itself required a connection onto the Michigan Central at Alger. The line's roots go back to the Lake Huron and Southwestern Railway (incorporated Apr 15 1878, opened Tawas City-Prescott that year), reorganized as the Tawas & Bay County Railroad in 1880, then sold in 1882 to lumber baron Russell Alger and rechartered as the Detroit, Bay City & Alpena on Apr 2 1883. It reached Au Sable by 1883, Black River by 1886, and Alpena itself by 1894 -- the same year it went into foreclosure. Reorganized in 1896 as the Detroit & Mackinac Railway (not covered by this file). GEOMETRY METHODOLOGY: real-traced through OpenStreetMap active/abandoned-rail data (Overpass API, shortest-path graph search) where fragments survive -- this is sparse rural logging-railroad country and much of the original alignment is gone, so the traced path (140.1 km / 87.1 mi) follows the best-available remnants rather than a precise historic centerline; it does not track as closely through every named 1880s station (e.g. Prescott) as the better-documented lines elsewhere on this map.
metadata.source: michiganrailroads.com (Detroit, Bay City and Alpena Railroad Company; Bay City and Alpena Railroad Company; Opening of the Detroit, Bay City & Alpena; Funding the Bay City and Alpena Railroad), american-rails.com (Detroit and Mackinac Railway)
